Elise still walked to the pier most afternoons after school. The gate was chained, but the chain had rusted through on one side and swung open if you lifted it just right. One afternoon in late October a man in waders set out across the flats toward the island, walking straight for the place where the channel cut deepest and filled first.

Elise did not call out. She climbed onto the booth's roof, took off her red scarf, and held it out sideways, the way her mother had once signaled the last boat to wait.

The man stopped, looked, and angled north toward the sandbar.

Later he came back along the pier, dripping to the knee.

"Is the crossing still watched?" he asked.

Elise thought of the onions in the ticket box and said, "Only by habit.""}
